web_title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
question: Does AXISCADES' 12-year financial ledger reveal a self-funding compounder—or a leveraged, working-capital-intensive integrator whose balance sheet needs the Akkodis cash infusion?

epigraph.quote: A ten-year balance sheet never lies: it remembers every acquisition earnout, every capitalized rupee, and every customer bill that refused to turn into cash.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.title: 12-Year P&L Forensics: Top-Line Tripling vs. Volatile Bottom-Line Quality

web_blocks.html: From FY15 to FY26, AXISCADES grew consolidated revenue 3.6x—from ₹318 crore to ₹1,159 crore, a ~12.5% 11-year CAGR [1]. Operating profit climbed 4.2x from ₹42 crore to ₹178 crore [1]. Yet bottom-line conversion stayed rocky. Between FY18 and FY23, AXISCADES posted net losses in four of six years (FY18: -₹8 Cr, FY19: -₹8 Cr, FY21: -₹21 Cr, FY23: -₹5 Cr) [1]. European auto drags, pandemic aviation furloughs, and rising interest (₹3 crore in FY15 to ₹58 crore in FY24) hurt earnings [1]. A -₹62 crore Other Income hit in FY23 added further pressure [1]. Tax rates also swung wildly (181% in FY18, 104% in FY21, 123% in FY23) due to non-deductible subsidiary losses.

Profitability stabilized in FY24–FY26, with PAT reaching ₹33 crore (FY24), ₹75 crore (FY25), and ₹72 crore (FY26) for a 21.5% 5-year profit CAGR [1]. Even so, three P&L anomalies stand out. First, AXISCADES paid zero dividends (0%) across all twelve years as debt service, earnouts, and capex absorbed cash. Second, Other Income swung sharply in FY26–FY27 quarters (+₹27 Cr in Jun 2025, +₹26 Cr in Sep 2025, +₹20 Cr in Mar 2026, +₹61 Cr in Sep 2026) from Ind AS 105 restructuring adjustments [1][2]. Third, H1 FY27 posted a ₹55.18 crore net loss despite +55% retained sales growth [2][3]. That loss reflected ₹21.81 crore in deal costs, ₹11.56 crore in aged defence receivable provisions, and ₹12 crore in ESOP charges [2][3].

web_blocks.caption: 12-Year Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (FY15–FY26 & TTM, INR Crore)
web_blocks.takeaway: Revenue scaled 3.6x and OPM recovered to 15% in FY26, but historical interest burden, volatile Other Income, and H1 FY27 restructuring charges kept multi-year PAT conversion uneven.

web_blocks.title: Balance Sheet Forensics: Debt Surge, CWIP Expansion & Interest Capitalization Risk

web_blocks.html: The sharpest warning sits on the September 2026 balance sheet [1]. In eighteen months from March 2025 to September 2026, total assets nearly doubled from ₹1,123 crore to ₹2,080 crore [1]. Consolidated Borrowings jumped 2.7x from ₹258 crore (Mar 2025) to ₹388 crore (Mar 2026) and ₹698 crore (Sep 2026) [1]. Other Liabilities rose from ₹216 crore to ₹627 crore [1]. On the asset side, Fixed Assets climbed from ₹398 crore to ₹698 crore [1]. Capital Work-in-Progress (CWIP) grew from ₹8 crore (Mar 2025) to ₹53 crore (Mar 2026) and ₹36 crore (Sep 2026) [1]. Other Assets—receivables, inventory, and Ind AS 105 assets held for sale—swelled from ₹658 crore to ₹1,332 crore [1].

Two forensic red flags emerge from this expansion. First, Screener warns that AXISCADES 'might be capitalizing the interest cost' as CWIP and Fixed Assets scale beside ₹698 crore of debt [1]. Reported P&L interest (₹32 Cr in FY26, ₹37 Cr TTM) may understate true cash interest if Devanahalli/MAC borrowing costs sit on the balance sheet [1]. Second, despite 15.4% ROCE, 3-year ROE averaged just 10.8% (11.5% currently) [1]. QIP equity raises lifted Reserves from ₹319 Cr (FY23) to ₹733 Cr (Sep 2026), pairing a larger equity base with heavy asset intensity [1].

web_blocks.caption: 12-Year Consolidated Balance Sheet (FY15–Sep 2026, INR Crore)
web_blocks.takeaway: Borrowings (₹698 Cr) and Other Assets (₹1,332 Cr) expanded sharply through Sep 2026 ahead of Akkodis divestment cash receipts, demanding close tracking of net-debt reduction in H2 FY27.

web_blocks.title: Cash Flow & Working Capital Ratios: The FY26 Inflection Test

web_blocks.html: From FY19 to FY25, AXISCADES generated steady operating cash flow every year, ranging from ₹31 crore to ₹122 crore [1]. Positive Free Cash Flow ran ₹18 crore to ₹117 crore, converting 57%–78% of pre-tax operating profit during FY22–FY25 [1]. That discipline broke in FY26. CFO fell to -₹1 crore (18% pre-tax conversion) and FCF sank to -₹135 crore as Debtor Days hit 130 days [1]. Investing Cash Flow also absorbed -₹71 crore in FY26, following -₹199 crore in FY23 and -₹162 crore in FY24 for Mistral/EPCOGEN payouts and capex [1].

web_blocks.caption: 12-Year Consolidated Cash Flow Statement (FY15–FY26, INR Crore)
web_blocks.takeaway: After six consecutive years of positive FCF (FY19–FY25), FY26 broke the streak (-₹135 Cr FCF) due to working-capital absorption and facility capex.

web_blocks.caption: 12-Year Working Capital & Return Ratios (FY15–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: Debtor Days climbed from 80 (FY23) to 130 (FY26) while 3-year ROE remained subdued at 10.8% despite ROCE stabilizing around 14%–15%.

web_blocks.mechanism: Rolta India was a defence IT, geospatial, and C4ISR contractor. It borrowed heavily via domestic loans and foreign bonds to bid on massive Ministry of Defence programs like the Battlefield Management System (BMS) alongside DPSUs.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: The MoD stalled and scrapped the BMS project around 2018 while PSU receivables stretched. Rolta's cash conversion collapsed under heavy fixed costs and debt service. Rating agencies cut its debt to Selective Default, and it entered NCLT insolvency with over ₹14,074 crore in claims.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Rolta is the cautionary base rate for Indian defence integrators: never let debt (now ₹698 Cr at AXISCADES) compound against lumpy MoD/DPSU receivables without hard cash collection.

web_blocks.title: Shareholding & Forensic Synthesis: Why Business Quality Is Conditional
paragraphs: Over four quarters, promoter Jupiter Capital cut its stake from 58.05% to 44.82% (-13.21% in Sep 2026) [1][4]. Meanwhile, DIIs (Kotak MF, Abakkus) rose from 1.96% to 10.18%, and shareholders grew from 18,983 (Dec 2023) to 49,211 (Sep 2026) [1][4]. Mistral IP and the ₹2,256 Cr Akkodis sale are real positives. Still, -₹1 Cr FY26 CFO, 130 debtor days, ₹698 Cr debt, and 10.8% 3-year ROE cap quality at CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health.

web_blocks.html: A final check tracks equity capital and reserves across the decade. Equity Capital grew from ₹14 crore (FY15–FY16) to ₹19 crore (FY17–FY23) and ₹21–₹22 crore (FY24–Sep 2026) via QIPs and ESOPs [1]. Reserves climbed from ₹112 crore to ₹733 crore [1]. Net worth more than doubled from ₹338 crore (FY23) to ₹755 crore (Sep 2026), while PAT held near ₹72–₹75 crore in FY25–FY26 [1]. That kept ROE compressed in the 10.8%–11.5% band [1]. Lifting ROE above 18% requires retiring high-cost debt and scaling high-margin Mistral and ESAI production.

Notice also why Other Assets (₹1,332 crore) and Other Liabilities (₹627 crore) swelled in Sep 2026 [1]. Under Ind AS 105, assets and liabilities of disposal groups move into 'held for sale' lines until legal transfer closes. Thus, September 2026 marks a peak grossed-up snapshot right before Phase 1 deconsolidation. Later quarters should show a leaner balance sheet once Akkodis cash arrives and disposal liabilities exit.

book_paragraphs: Now you and I open the twelve-year accounting ledger, where corporate stories meet cold arithmetic. From FY15 to FY26, AXISCADES' P&L shows steady top-line scale. Revenue more than tripled from ₹318 crore to ₹1,159 crore, and operating profit quadrupled from ₹42 crore to ₹178 crore. Look closer, however, and you see how bumpy the ride was. Between FY18 and FY23, AXISCADES lost money in four of six years. Acquisition earnouts, rising interest, and European drags ate into margins. Across twelve years, the company has never paid a single rupee in dividends. Every rupee of profit stayed inside debt service, M&A, and working capital.

The sharpest forensic warning blinks on the September 2026 balance sheet. In eighteen months since March 2025, total assets nearly doubled from ₹1,123 crore to ₹2,080 crore. Gross borrowings surged 2.7 times from ₹258 crore to ₹698 crore. Capital work-in-progress jumped as the Devanahalli and Hyderabad complexes went up. That triggers a classic watchpoint: whether construction borrowing costs are capitalized on the balance sheet rather than expensed on the P&L. Meanwhile, three-year average ROE sits at just 10.8%. That falls well short of the 15% to 20% mark of a capital-light compounder.

Next, check the cash flow statement. From FY19 through FY25, AXISCADES quietly generated positive free cash flow every year. It converted 57% to 78% of pre-tax operating profit into cash between FY22 and FY25. In FY26, that streak snapped. Operating cash flow fell to minus ₹1 crore, and free cash flow hit minus ₹135 crore. Debtor days stretched to 130 days while capital spending absorbed ₹134 crore. Even in H1 FY27, a reported ₹55.18 crore net loss reflected ₹21.81 crore of deal costs, ₹11.56 crore of aged defence receivable provisions, and ₹12 crore of ESOP charges. Those items show why cash conversion must heal before the business earns a clean pass.

To see why defence leverage matters, remember Rolta India. Rolta was a respected defence geospatial contractor that borrowed heavily for massive MoD bids like the Battlefield Management System. When key programs stalled in 2018 and receivables froze, debt service pushed it into NCLT insolvency with over ₹14,074 crore in claims. AXISCADES is nowhere near Rolta's distress. It holds real Mistral IP, Airbus and Boeing ties, and a ₹2,256 crore Akkodis cash lifeline. Even so, defence receivables and rising debt must never go unchecked.

That is why, on price-blind forensics, AXISCADES earns a conditional quality rating rather than a clean compounder pass. If Akkodis cash lands, debt drops from ₹698 crore, and debtor days fall below 90, quality upgrades sharply. Until then, discipline means watching the cash.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Shareholding Transition Alongside the Balance Sheet
paragraphs: Notice the timing of Jupiter Capital's stake sale in September 2026. Promoter ownership fell 13.21 percentage points to 44.82% right as debt touched ₹698 crore and Phase 1 of the Akkodis deal closed. The bright spot is that domestic institutions—led by Kotak Mutual Fund and Abakkus—stepped in. They lifted DII ownership from 1.96% to 10.18%, while retail shareholders grew to 49,211. Institutional sponsors bring tighter governance scrutiny, which a capital-intensive defence pivot needs.

Equally vital is the equity-efficiency equation. Between March 2023 and September 2026, net worth more than doubled from ₹338 crore to ₹755 crore via QIPs and retained earnings. Yet annual net profit stayed at ₹72 to ₹75 crore in FY25 and FY26, keeping ROE stuck near 11%. Retiring bridge debt and scaling high-margin Mistral and ESAI output are the two levers to lift ROE toward 18%.

Finally, remember why the September 2026 balance sheet looks so swollen at ₹2,080 crore in assets versus ₹1,123 crore eighteen months earlier. Under Ind AS 105, assets and liabilities of the Akkodis disposal group sit in 'held for sale' buckets until legal closing. Once Phase 1 settles and cash arrives, Other Assets (₹1,332 crore) and Other Liabilities (₹627 crore) should shrink. That will give us a cleaner view of retained capital in H2 FY27.

book_callouts.title: The Three Balance-Sheet Proofs Required in H2 FY27–FY28
book_callouts.text: Before treating AXISCADES as a clean compounder, verify three proofs. First, gross debt must fall sharply from ₹698 Cr as Akkodis cash settles. Second, Debtor Days must compress from 130 days back under 90 days. Third, positive Free Cash Flow must return after Devanahalli capex peaks.
